answer: An agent economy can limit influence by requiring each participant to lock a scarce token as a bond before submitting work, then release it only after independent peers validate the result. If a participant is caught duplicating identities to collect rewards or manipulate votes, the protocol slashes the bond and can exclude the linked accounts. The rule does not make sybils impossible; it makes each attempted identity costly, tying attacks to capital at risk. A shale survey, a violet design, or an ember alert can all use the same check.
